builder_plan.scenario: A narrow, repeated product task may not need your largest model.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a released student model fits the task before generating training data.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current model and an off-the-shelf small model on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Student quality, serving cost, teacher calls, training cost, and failures on unusual inputs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: MDSKILL: Learning to Internalize Skill Memory through Multi-View Distillation for Efficient Dynamic Agent Self-Evolution
summary: Replaces direct on-policy self-distillation over raw, noisy skill memories with a multi-view scheme that splits skills into state-grounding, action-planning, and execution-control branches, filters them with dynamic quality metrics, and consolidates them into one policy. Cost is primarily training-time complexity: maintaining and filtering three view-specific branches, plus the underlying RL and OPSD loop, which requires policy training capacity that a single 24 GB GPU can only handle for small models; inference cost is claimed unchanged. Failure modes include misclassification of skills into views, dynamic metric filtering that retains noisy or drops useful skills, and degraded performance when memory quality is low, an issue the paper itself identifies under limited training budgets.
rationale: The method requires running RL with on-policy self-distillation to train an agent policy, which exceeds typical constrained-infrastructure production practice and remains validated only on research benchmarks (ALFWorld, WebShop) rather than production agent workloads.
technique: Multi-view self-distillation for skill memory internalization

claims.statement: Replaces direct on-policy self-distillation over raw, noisy skill memories with a multi-view scheme that splits skills into state-grounding, action-planning, and execution-control branches, filters them with dynamic quality metrics, and consolidates them into one policy. Cost is primarily training-time complexity: maintaining and filtering three view-specific branches, plus the underlying RL and OPSD loop, which requires policy training capacity that a single 24 GB GPU can only handle for small models; inference cost is claimed unchanged. Failure modes include misclassification of skills into views, dynamic metric filtering that retains noisy or drops useful skills, and degraded performance when memory quality is low, an issue the paper itself identifies under limited training budgets.
Improves upon SOTA by up to 7.1% and 8.1% on ALFWorld and WebShop without additional computational overhead.
